CANCEL_SCOPE_RULE: USER_LOCKS.per_card_cancel puts the control on the in-flight row, but the endpoint is queue-level (POST /{queue}/cancel). The user-visible accessible name MUST therefore be CANCEL_CONTROL_LABEL and the title CANCEL_CONTROL_TITLE; any CANCEL_LABEL_FORBIDDEN string as the accessible name is a defect, because a row-local control that reads `Cancel` lets a person stop the whole queue believing they stopped one item (reviewer R4-F3). The mockup's own tooltip was already scope-bearing; the AC now matches it. The disclosure lives entirely in the label and title -- see CANCEL_CONFIRM_POLICY, which forbids gating the action behind a dialog.
REQUEUE_BLOCKER_POLICY: Re-queue from a BLOCKER state is not a generic reset. QualityBlocked -> Pending MUST first apply the current downloader defaults to the job (the apply_defaults_to_pending mapping: quality, audio_format, audio_only) and then re-evaluate `_incompatible(job)` against the live SABR snapshot; if the job is still incompatible while SABR mode is Active the job stays QualityBlocked and the route answers REQUEUE_BLOCKER_CONFLICT_CODE naming BLOCKER_REMEDIATION[QualityBlocked]. Without this, a reset re-enters the Pending pool that the worker drains, and `_run_one` does not re-run apply_lock -- so Retry would defeat the very quality guard that created the block (reviewer R4-F2, confirmed against services/download.py apply_lock/_run_one). AgeRestricted -> Pending is unconditional: cookie/auth options are read at execution time, so a settings change is enough. Cancelled and Failed -> Pending stay unconditional.

BLOCKER_REMEDIATION.QualityBlocked: Settings > Downloader > Quality (choose a lower quality, or a supported audio format for audio-only jobs)
BLOCKER_REMEDIATION.AgeRestricted: Settings > Cookies & Authentication (sign-in required for this video)

BLOCKER_META_RULE: A card in a BLOCKER_STATUSES state MUST render, in its meta zone, both the blocker reason (the job's error_message) and BLOCKER_REMEDIATION[status] -- the setting the user has to change. Retry on a blocker row without that copy looks broken when it legitimately refuses (reviewer R4-F2).

KEBAB_MENU_ORDER_SEMANTICS: KEBAB_MENU_ORDER is a list of ACTION IDS fixing the RELATIVE ORDER of the actions that are both supplied as callbacks and applicable under KEBAB_AVAILABILITY -- it is not a required membership list. An action is omitted entirely (never rendered disabled, never a no-op) when its callback is not supplied or when KEBAB_AVAILABILITY excludes it for the row's state/position; the reviewer confirmed absence is the right interaction, because disabled rows add keyboard stops without helping. The surviving actions render in KEBAB_MENU_ORDER order, each with its KEBAB_ACTION_LABELS entry (copy-location's label is state-dependent per R5-F4). Availability is evaluated PER ACTION, never per group: a first-but-not-last row still offers move-down and move-bottom, and only a single-item queue drops all four move actions (reviewer R5-F2, which caught an expected set that would have silently removed two promised operations from the top row of every multi-item queue).

KEBAB_AVAILABILITY.move-up: the row is not first in the list

BLOCKER_REASON_RULE: Every job that ENTERS a BLOCKER_STATUSES state must carry a human-readable reason in error_message at the moment of the transition, rendered from BLOCKER_REASON_TEMPLATE[status], and BLOCKER_REASON_INVARIANT must then hold for the rest of that job's life. AgeRestricted already satisfies entry: services/download.py:506-507 catches AgeRestrictedError and calls _finish(..., error=str(exc)), and adapter.py:392/446 raises it with the template text. QualityBlocked does not, at entry or afterwards -- see BLOCKER_REASON_PRODUCERS for the exact sites in each of the three phases. Without entry coverage the reason BLOCKER_META_RULE requires does not exist in production data, so AC-44.15 could only ever pass against a fabricated component prop while a real blocked user sees an empty explanation (reviewer R5-F1); without the invariant the reason exists but drifts or outlives its own status (reviewer R6-F1).

copy-location._why: reviewer R5-F4: one canonical action id and one order slot, but the visible label must name what actually lands on the clipboard. Before an output path exists the action copies the source URL, so a menu item reading 'Copy path' would lie about its own result. The proposal writes the action as 'Copy path/URL' (proposal:78) and the mockup renders it 'Copy URL' (mockup:287) - the state-dependent label is the reading that satisfies both.

CANCEL_CONFIRM_POLICY: Queue-level Cancel takes NO confirmation dialog. proposal:146-149 places it on the destructive-action ladder explicitly as 'queue-level Cancel of a re-queueable job -> no dialog (re-queue is cheap)'; ConfirmModal is reserved for Remove and Clear. Round 5 briefly required a confirm step as part of the cancel-wording fix; the reviewer rejected that (R5-F3) because it adds unchosen friction to a time-sensitive stop and contradicts the presentational onCancelQueue contract. Scope is disclosed by CANCEL_CONTROL_LABEL and CANCEL_CONTROL_TITLE at the affordance itself, which is the whole point of locking those two strings.
BLOCKER_REASON_COPY_RULE: BLOCKER_REASON_TEMPLATE strings are QUALITY-INDEPENDENT and acronym-free: they interpolate no job field, so no persisted reason can contradict the row it sits on, and they name no internal term the user has never seen. Round 6's QualityBlocked template did both wrong -- it formatted {quality} into the sentence and it exposed 'SABR' (reviewer R6-F1). Formatting a mutable job field into a stored sentence is what made the reason go stale, because apply_defaults_to_pending rewrites quality/audio_format/audio_only on an already-blocked row without touching error_message (services/download.py:369-391). Removing the interpolation collapses the whole maintenance problem from 'recompute the reason at every mutation' to 'ensure the reason is present' -- which is why BLOCKER_REASON_INVARIANT is an ensure-present invariant, not a recompute-on-write rule. The job-specific detail the user needs is already on the card: the quality is in the meta zone and the fix is in BLOCKER_REMEDIATION.
BLOCKER_REASON_INVARIANT: PERSISTED-STATE INVARIANT, not a per-callsite patch: (1) every DownloadJob persisted with status QualityBlocked carries a non-empty error_message equal to BLOCKER_REASON_TEMPLATE['QualityBlocked']; (2) no job persisted OUT of a BLOCKER_STATUSES state retains a blocker reason. Clause (1) must hold for rows that were already blocked before this MEU shipped, not only for rows created after it -- a legacy reasonless row is exactly the row a user is looking at when they wonder why nothing is downloading. Clause (2) is the mirror: DownloadJob.transition is `replace(self, status=...)` and preserves error_message verbatim (domain/download.py:111-119), so without it a cleared SABR lock leaves every un-blocked job displaying the reason it was blocked for. ENFORCEMENT is the three mechanisms in BLOCKER_REASON_ENFORCEMENT, not a list of service callsites: Round 7 stated this invariant while enforcing it only in apply_lock and apply_defaults_to_pending, which an upgrading user may never trigger -- so the promise outran its enforcer and a legacy row reached the card blank, including immediately after a refused Retry (reviewer R7-F1). An invariant over persisted state has to be enforced where state is persisted.
CLICKABLE_REGION_RULE: The card's role="button" open-region contains NO interactive descendant. Every id in CARD_INTERACTIVE_ZONES renders as a SIBLING of that region inside the card container, never inside it, and activating any of them never invokes onOpen. The mockup's markup does not satisfy this on its own: it nests the primary action and the kebab trigger inside <div class="body"> (mockup:261-277), which proposal SS4 is what carries role="button" -- only the checkbox is already a sibling, and only the checkbox had an AC proving it (AC-44.2). The mockup's own zone strip (mockup:278) already lays out 'action' and the kebab as separate right-edge columns, so hoisting them out of the open-region is layout-neutral: the visual design is unchanged and only the DOM ancestry differs. Nesting them would give a keyboard or screen-reader user a Retry that also opens the item through bubbling, and would strip the descendants of independent name/role/value -- the axe `nested-interactive` failure, WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2, and the reason the HTML spec forbids interactive content inside <button> (reviewer R6-F2).

BLOCKER_REASON_ENFORCEMENT.boundary-normalizer: domain/download.py gains BLOCKER_REASONS (status -> reason text, the code-side home of BLOCKER_REASON_TEMPLATE) and a pure normalize_blocker_reason(job) -> DownloadJob that returns the job with BLOCKER_REASON_INVARIANT satisfied: it fills a blank error_message when the status is in BLOCKER_REASONS, and clears error_message when the status is NOT a blocker state AND the current message is exactly one of the BLOCKER_REASONS values. That second condition is deliberately narrow -- an unconditional clear would erase a Failed job's real traceback. infrastructure/.../repositories.py calls it in SqlAlchemyDownloadRepository.add and .save, which are the ONLY two write paths into download_jobs (reorder touches queue_position, delete removes rows, bulk reset_failed selects Failed only). Enforcing there rather than at service callsites is the whole point: no future service, route, or MCP handler can persist a reasonless blocked row by forgetting to, and the four per-callsite writes Round 7 planned in services/download.py are DELETED as redundant (reviewer R7-F1: 'centralize future DownloadJob add/save validation or normalization at the domain/persistence boundary').
BLOCKER_REASON_ENFORCEMENT.upgrade-backfill: infrastructure/.../migrations.py appends one idempotent UPDATE that fills error_message for existing QualityBlocked rows with a NULL or blank message. MIGRATIONS is an append-only list run by apply_migrations() at engine init, before any route can list a job, so an upgrading user's queue is repaired before they ever see it -- which the boundary normalizer alone cannot do, because a legacy row is never re-saved until something happens to touch it. Re-running matches zero rows, so it is idempotent in the same way the CREATE IF NOT EXISTS statements around it are. The SQL literal is built from BLOCKER_REASONS at import, never retyped, per the single-statement rule.
BLOCKER_REASON_ENFORCEMENT.refusal-canonicalization: the AC-42.10 still-incompatible Retry path persists the job through the normalizing save before answering REQUEUE_BLOCKER_CONFLICT_CODE, instead of writing nothing. Belt-and-braces behind the migration, and it closes the reviewer's sharpest case: the blank card surviving the one action a confused user actually takes.

BLOCKER_REASON_MIGRATION_PREDICATE: status = 'QualityBlocked' AND (error_message IS NULL OR TRIM(error_message) = '')
